entries.title: SHA-512 and SHA-512-Half ledger / transaction hashing
entries.primitive: SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4), SHA-512-Half = first 256 bits of SHA-512
entries.notes: SHA-512-Half is the ledger's core hash (digest.h: basic_sha512_half_hasher): transaction signing digests, ledger entry indexes, feature IDs. Implemented via OpenSSL low-level SHA512_Init/Update/Final (digest.cpp:58-78), deprecated in OpenSSL 3.x but present in the pinned OpenSSL 1.1.1w.

entries.title: SHA-256 hashing
entries.notes: Used inside hash160 (RIPEMD160(SHA-256)) for account IDs and for the self-signed default TLS certificate (X509_sign with EVP_sha256, make_SSLContext.cpp:233). Implemented via OpenSSL low-level SHA256_* (digest.cpp:84+).

entries.title: RIPEMD-160 in account-ID derivation (hash160)
entries.notes: hash160 = RIPEMD-160(SHA-256(pubkey)) (include/xrpl/protocol/digest.h:155-157). 160-bit output gives ~80-bit Grover-era strength. The tree's own comment (AccountID.cpp:145-156) debates this choice. Implemented via OpenSSL low-level RIPEMD160_* (digest.cpp:29-52), removed in OpenSSL 3.x default provider — a hard blocker for any OpenSSL 3 migration.

entries.title: TLS for peer / RPC / WebSocket ports (OpenSSL via Boost.Asio)
entries.notes: Default cipher list is "TLSv1.2:!CBC:!DSS:!PSK:!eNULL:!aNULL" (make_SSLContext.cpp:104); renegotiation disabled (line 375). Key exchange is ECDHE via OpenSSL/Boost.Asio defaults — NO explicit curve or ECDH configuration exists in src/ or include/, so the negotiated groups are library defaults (unverified which). No TLS 1.3 or min/max protocol version setting exists in the tree (grep: zero hits), so TLS 1.3 availability is UNVERIFIED, not claimed on or off. No PQ KEM.

entries.title: Self-signed default TLS certificate (ephemeral RSA-2048)
entries.primitive: RSA-2048 (ephemeral, generated at startup), X.509 self-signed, SHA-256
entries.notes: When no certificate/key is configured, postfiatd generates a 2048-bit RSA key at startup (make_SSLContext.cpp:66, 120) and a self-signed certificate with EVP_sha256() (line 233). RSA-2048 is Shor-vulnerable; the certificate is self-signed (no chain of trust) by design for the default case.

entries.title: Peer handshake channel binding (SHA-512 of TLS Finished)
entries.primitive: SHA-512 over TLS Finished messages (non-standard construction)
evidence: src/xrpld/overlay/detail/Handshake.cpp:128: hashLastMessage(SSL const* ssl, size_t (*get)(const SSL*, void*, size_t))
entries.notes: Cookie = SHA-512(local Finished) XOR/combined with SHA-512(peer Finished) (src/xrpld/overlay/detail/Handshake.cpp:128-160), then signed with the node key. The code itself notes this is non-standard and cites openssl/openssl#5509 and ripple/rippled#2413. Binding strength inherits SHA-512's Grover reduction and the underlying TLS key exchange's Shor vulnerability.

entries.title: Cryptographically secure RNG (OpenSSL RAND_bytes)
entries.primitive: CSPRNG: OpenSSL RAND_bytes, seeded via RAND_poll + std::random_device
evidence: src/libxrpl/crypto/csprng.cpp:80: // RAND_bytes is thread-safe on OpenSSL 1.1.0 and later when compiled
entries.notes: csprng_engine (src/libxrpl/crypto/csprng.cpp:37-92): RAND_poll at startup, extra std::random_device entropy via RAND_add, RAND_bytes for output, throws on failure. Used for secret-key generation (SecretKey.cpp:301) and secp256k1 nonce material via the library. Entropy quality depends on the OS/OpenSSL DRBG, not on any post-quantum primitive.

entries.title: Deterministic key derivation from 128-bit seeds
evidence: include/xrpl/protocol/SecretKey.h:132: generateSecretKey(KeyType type, Seed const& seed);
src/libxrpl/protocol/SecretKey.cpp:309: generateSecretKey(KeyType type, Seed const& seed)
src/libxrpl/protocol/SecretKey.cpp:379: auto const sk = generateSecretKey(type, seed);
src/test/app/Manifest_test.cpp:564: auto const sk = generateSecretKey(KeyType::ed25519, randomSeed());
entries.notes: Ed25519 keys: SHA-512-Half(seed). secp256k1 keys: SHA-512-based root-key derivation with a 32-bit sequence counter (SecretKey.cpp:86-124, 309-327). A 128-bit seed gives at most 128-bit classical entropy regardless of the hash; Grover does not reduce seed entropy below the seed size, but the derived keys are still ECDLP keys (see CRYPTO-01/02). RFC 1751 word-list encoding of seeds exists (src/libxrpl/crypto/RFC1751.cpp).

entries.title: Validator manifests (ephemeral signing-key rotation)
entries.primitive: Ed25519 or secp256k1 signatures over validator manifests
evidence: src/test/app/Manifest_test.cpp:244: m.serialized, m.masterKey, m.signingKey, m.sequence, m.domain);
src/xrpld/app/misc/Manifest.h:163: `Manifest::verify` should be called after constructing manifest.
entries.notes: Validator manifests carry a master key, an ephemeral signing key, and signatures over both (src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/Manifest.cpp:46-145). Revocation manifests rotate/revoke keys. Manifest trust is the validator-list trust root; a Shor break of the manifest key type would let an attacker forge validator identity. No PQ signature in manifests.

entries.title: gRPC API transport (ETL for Clio)
entries.notes: The gRPC server binds with InsecureServerCredentials() (src/xrpld/app/main/GRPCServer.cpp:572), with the comment 'Listen on the given address without any authentication mechanism.' The example config documents the port as ETL for Clio with a secure_gateway IP allowlist (cfg/postfiatd-example.cfg, [port_grpc]). No TLS option exists in the gRPC server code. Exposure is a deployment-topology decision, not a library version issue.
